title: The Honey of Contemplation and the Blood of Justice
english: But friends. 'And provoke,' he says, through prayers and supplications, 'and [say] I will pray for my friend': 'Keep me, Lord, from the hand of a sinner' (Ps 118:4) and 'deliver me from an unrighteous man' (Ps 140:5) and 'do not deliver me into the hands of those who afflict me, because for your sake we are being killed all day long; we have been counted as sheep for the slaughter' (Ps 44:22).

Do not give sleep to your eyes, nor let a watchman stand over your eyelids. Sleep is sin in its activity; but drowsiness is the first unclean thought established in the soul. Therefore also before drowsiness, the Law prevents sleep: 'For it was said,' he says, 'to the ancients: You shall not murder' (Ex 20:13); but I say: You shall not be angry. And here, for it seems to me, the Law prevents sleep, but the Gospel of Christ prevents drowsiness, if indeed the one cuts off sin in its activity, while the other [cuts off] the evil first established according to the intellect.

Go to the ant, O sluggard, and observe its ways and become wiser than it (Prov 6:6); for even without a farmer being there, and not having one to compel him, and not being under a master, it prepares its food for the summer. Note here that it calls the natural and harmonious movement of the ant wisdom; for indeed the wiser is called wiser than the wise. And how could it not be under a master, if all things are slaves of God? Or is God ever called a master in two ways, as Creator and as known? Therefore also Paul writes: 'But now, having been freed from sin, having become slaves to God' (Rom 6:22), clearly according to virtue and knowledge, 'have your fruit unto sanctification, the end being eternal life.' And if the ant is unworthy of such an end, being irrational, it clearly is also free from such a slavery; so it is well said that the ant is not under a master according to this [type of] mastery, but is again under a master as having God as Creator.

Go to the bee... of which kings and commoners bring their labors for health. Through the ant, it seems Solomon outlines the practical way for us, but through the bee, he signifies the contemplation of events and of the one who did them, which both the pure and the impure, and the wise and the un-

They are brought toward the health of the soul. And it seems to me that the herald of these things holds the word of the matter, but the honey remaining to him is a symbol of their contemplation. For the herald will pass away: 'for the heaven and the earth, he says, will pass away' (Matt 24:35); but the honey will not pass away. For neither will the words of our Savior Christ pass away, concerning which Solomon says: 'Words sweet as honey are good, and their sweetness is healing to the soul' (Prov 16:24); and David: 'How sweet, he says, are your words to my throat, sweeter than honey to my mouth' (Ps 19:10).

The result of the labor is named labor. Until when, sluggard, will you lie down? When will you arise from sleep? This sleep only happens to a rational soul; for here it signifies wickedness and ignorance, of which watchfulness makes something 'like a sparrow chirping on a roof.' Poverty happens to you like an evil traveler, and want like a good runner. Poverty is a deprivation of knowledge; and want is a scarcity of virtues.

He himself blows with the eye, but it signifies the foot, and he teaches by blowing with the fingers. Beware here, lest the opponents, through such movements of the body, recognize their own thoughts being nourished in us, since we have believed only God to be the Knower of Hearts. An eye of insolence, an unjust tongue, hands pouring out righteous blood. Everyone who eats the flesh of Christ and drinks his blood acquires righteous blood, the deprivation of which is said to cause a rational soul to die; 'for the soul, he says, that sins shall die' (Ezek 18:4).

And if there is righteous blood, it is evident that there is also unjust blood, which those who devour the given food among the Ethiopians gather within themselves and are nourished by the bread of falsehood, consume. And those sacrificing to foreign gods consume their own righteous blood; but those offering themselves as a sacrifice to the only God destroy unjust blood. And certainly, the generation of righteous blood will follow the corruption of unjust blood, and the generation of unjust blood will follow the corruption of righteous blood. But this is destined to happen now; from the beginning it was not so; for righteousness did not come about through the corruption of wickedness, just as health does not come about through the corruption of disease, of the...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Theft, Adultery, and the Nature of Wisdom
english: Children being formed with health from the beginning. A false witness kindles lies and sends judgments among brothers. Brothers are those having the gift of adoption and being under the same father, Christ, whom the witness of injustice attempts to divide, casting tribulations and judgments among them.

And 'kindles', I think, is placed because of the passionate thoughts igniting the mind toward anger and hatred, and desire toward shameful works. These thoughts the holy Paul also named the fiery arrows of the evil one, piercing the soul and working death (Ephesians 6:16).

'Guard, son, the laws of your father and do not reject the statutes of your mother...' (Proverbs 6:20-22). Whenever you walk, lead her, and let her be with you. The mother is proposed to be led, who is the wisdom having begotten us according to God. Yet it was necessary for him to say the father; for he is more suitable for being in union with the son. But since it is not possible for him to know God before the contemplation of things having happened, for this reason he proposes the mother and not the father to be led, so that through the mother the son might see the father; for if she does not himself beget him, he does not see the light, which is the knowledge of him, the God.

That the commandment of the law is a lamp and light and way of life, a reproof and instruction. That the commandment of the law is a lamp and light. And perhaps the Old Testament is a lamp: 'for he was the lamp that was burning and shining' (Zechariah 4:6); but the New Testament is light: 'for I, he says, am the light of the world' (John 8:12).
For the honor of a prostitute is as much as one loaf. For such is the pleasure of wickedness as much as one loaf.

Will someone release fire in his bosom and not burn his clothes? Or will someone walk upon coals of fire and burn his feet? This one releases the fire in the bosom, the one forgiving the unchaste thought in the heart, corrupting the righteous thoughts through lingering. And this one walks upon the coals, the one destroying his own soul through the energy of sin.

Thus the one who entered toward an unchaste woman will not be acquitted, nor everyone touching her. An unchaste woman speaks of wickedness; for the devil is the man of her, who begets with her the lawless sons.
And the Savior says in the Gospels to the Jews: 'You are of your father the devil' (John 8:44).

It is no wonder if someone catches a thief; for he steals in order to fill a hungry soul. If he is caught, he will pay sevenfold and, by giving all his possessions, he will save himself. But if he is caught by true knowledge, he will lay aside all false knowledge, he who formerly stole through the need of knowledge from the foolishness made mad by our Savior's wisdom.

And the adulteress, through the need of wits, procures destruction for her soul. Everyone who has shared in the evil of the adulteress is a partaker of the devil, the first who rejoiced in evil and who from the beginning has been a murderer.

For the mind of a man full of zeal for it will show no mercy in the day of judgment. There he shows that we will have the devil as an accuser of the things done to us in the day of judgment. And this also the holy Paul says: 'so that the one against us, having nothing to say, may appear nothing trivial concerning us' (2 Cor 4:2).

'Son, honor the Lord and you will be strong; but fear no other besides him' (Prov 3:21). If through the transgression of the law someone dishonors God, by doing so he makes it manifest that he dishonors the law and God.

I have said that your wisdom is a sister; make practical understanding known to yourself. Our sister is wisdom, because he who made the incorporeal nature is Father and has made this. And there he speaks of wisdom not as the Son of God, but as the contemplation of bodies and incorporeal things, and of the judgment and providence in them, the vision of which is understanding, and knowledge, and instruction, and discernment.
In order that he may keep you from an alien and evil woman, if she should strike you with words of charm. The words that strike with charm are passions of thought.

For peeping from a window of her house into the streets, seeing the youth of any of the foolish children, lacking in wits, passing by a corner in the passages of her house, and speaking in the evening darkness, whenever the nocturnal silence is thick, the woman meets him having a prostitute-like appearance, which causes the hearts of the young to fall away. He now calls the flesh of the man a window; for through this the evil one works his snares for those who wish to [do so].
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Exegesis of Proverbs
english: To walk the broad, spacious road that leads to destruction. But here, one must attend to what Solomon says concerning vice: that it does not lead a man initially onto the broad road, nor does it force him to walk through the passages of its house, or approach a corner, or speak in the evening darkness; rather, if he sees someone giving himself over to pleasures, there immediately 'an appearance having met him, it is a fornication, which causes the hearts of the young to wander' (Prov 7:5).

91 Nightly stillness and the dark, unclean state is what is called the soul's condition, through which, being unfolded, sin is accomplished through the body. 92 7, 12 For it wanders for a certain time outside, a time in the squares, sitting by every corner, 7, 13.1 then having taken hold, it loved him. Those wandering in the squares taking up thoughts of adultery, fornication, and theft; 8 but those wandering outside of these move according to nature, seeking the bed of men and taking up fantasies of other forbidden things.

93 If of the thoughts some are pure and others are unclean—and if of lines the straight ones are called straight, but the bent ones are not straight, a corner being a bent straight line—then an unclean thought is a mental corner. Therefore, vice sitting by every corner signifies its deceiving the soul through all the unclean thoughts. And a demonic passion is an impression moved toward shameful work, calling out the soul.

94 7, 15 'Because of this I went out to meet you; longing for your face, I have found you' (Prov 7:15); 7, 16 'I have spread my bed with curtains; I have made my couch with cushions of Egypt' (Prov 7:16); 7, 17 'I have torn my veil with saffron; my house with cinnamon' (Prov 7:17). Vice seeks to disgrace the face of our soul through the curtains, the bed, the cushions, the saffron, and the cinnamon, which are various evil passions as they occur according to the inventors of evils.

95 7, 19 'For my man is not at home; he has gone on a long journey' (Prov 7:19); 7, 20 'having taken a bag of silver in his hand; after many days he will return to his house' (Prov 7:20). If [it says] 'after many days he will return to his house,' Paul, having intensely scrutinized the economy, writes of the last enemy.

The overcoming of death. Regarding the one who followed it, having been seduced: there are three kinds of erithion, namely the kepphos, the white one, and the one called the asterias. Of these, the kepphos mates difficultly and pours out; for it both cries out and pours blood, as they say, letting it flow from the eyes, and it gives birth poorly and painfully. These things, indeed, we have set down from Aristotle's histories concerning animals.

But it seems that the Scripture has fashioned its wording from the history of the kepphos bird to mean the woman being persuaded by a prostitute, being seduced and becoming like a bird through lawlessness. [For example, being moved.] For having wounded many, it has cast down [them], and they are countless, whom it has murdered; Titroskes mocks us with thoughts, but it murders with sins.

For it is upon the high edges; and in the midst of the soft ones, courage stands between recklessness and cowardice. For it lies in wait by the gates of the powerful; and in the entrances it is praised. Wisdom is said to be praised sometimes in exits and sometimes in entrances, that is, beside those coming out from evil and entering into virtue; for he names the one coming out and the one entering as exit and entrance. Often we have noted this habit of his, that from the states he names those who possess the states, that is, the best ones or the worst ones.
Perceive, you who are without malice, the craftiness; but you who are uneducated, put a heart within you. Here, Cardia has spoken of virtue as that which accompanies the heart.

Take instruction and not silver, and knowledge instead of tested gold... For wisdom is better than precious stones. There, Wisdom took as a genus the instruction and the knowledge; for having placed instruction and knowledge before, she leads into it; 'for wisdom is better than precious stones' (Proverbs 8:11), as instruction and knowledge are contained within wisdom, which is first the gift of the Holy Spirit, if indeed 'a word of wisdom is given through the Spirit' (1 Corinthians 2:13). And this same thing is also called the spirit of adoption (Romans 8:15).

The fear of the Lord hates injustice, and insolence and pride, and the ways of the wicked (Proverbs 8:13). Note that he speaks of injustice and insolence and pride regarding the unrighteous, the insolent, and the proud, from the worst [ways].
